prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: DHT22_DATA is an OPEN. The F.Cu track from U1 pad 4 (16.51, 31.75) ends at (13.4, 29.12) and the B.Cu track that runs to the sensor starts at the same XY (13.4, 29.12), but there is NO via there: the net changes layer with no barrel. The Board IR is inconsistent in the same way - its track list jumps F.Cu->B.Cu at (13.4, 16.6) while its via list holds no via at that point (one DHT22_DATA via only, at (10.2, 19.0)). The MCU pin 4 (PD2) is therefore not connected to U2 pad 2 (DHT22 data); the only part of the net that is joined is U1 pad 4 to the R1 pull-up. The DHT22 can never be read. A zone refill does not close it.
expected: Every net is continuous copper; a change of layer is made by a via whose barrel lands on copper on both layers. U1 pin 4 and U2 pad 2 must be one net.
evidence: board_ir.json (tracks/vias); board_03.kicad_pcb: F.Cu segment (13.965685,29.685685)->(13.4,29.12) then B.Cu segment (13.4,29.12)->(10.765685,27.285685), no via at (13.4,29.12), plus a zero-length F.Cu segment at the via (10.2,26.72); .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/board_03_drc.json (my kicad-cli run) and the product's own artifacts/board_03/drc.json agree: 2x track_dangling (Track [DHT22_DATA] on F.Cu len 0.8000 mm at 13.965685,29.685685; on B.Cu len 0.5657 mm at 13.4,29.12) and unconnected_items 'Track [DHT22_DATA] on B.Cu (13.4,29.12) <-> Track [DHT22_DATA] on F.Cu (13.965685,29.685685)'.

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: U1 (ATMEGA328P-PU) pad 21 is AVCC and carries NO net; pad 20 (AREF) is tied to VCC_5V and pad 22 (AGND) to GND. The ATmega328P datasheet requires AVCC to be connected to VCC and requires AREF not to be driven above AVCC, so the analog block is left unpowered while the reference node is held at 5 V. There is no capacitor on AVCC either.
expected: AVCC (pin 21) tied to VCC_5V with a 100 nF decoupling capacitor at the pin; AREF either tied to AVCC through a 100 nF cap to GND (as the Arduino Uno does) or left unconnected, never driven above AVCC.
evidence: board_03.kicad_pcb U1: (pad "20" thru_hole ... (net "VCC_5V")), (pad "21" thru_hole ... no net), (pad "22" thru_hole ... (net "GND")); Microchip ATmega328P (DS40002061A) DIP-28 pin table: 20=AREF, 21=AVCC, 22=GND/AGND, 23=PC0/ADC0, and 'AVCC must be connected to VCC'.

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The board file's only zone (net GND, layer B.Cu, name 'plane GND') contains NO fill data - zero filled_polygon blocks. As shipped, GND is five separate copper islands (each GND via touches only its own pad) and the fabrication data carries no ground plane: Gerbers exported from the shipped file have a B.Cu layer with 7 flash operations (3,795 bytes); the same export with --check-zones (refill) has 3,032 flashes (78,830 bytes). The product's own DRC reports 5 via_dangling and 4 GND 'Missing connection between items' - all four GND opens and all five via_dangling warnings disappear as soon as the zone is refilled, which is how I separated this from F-0001.
expected: A board handed to a fab carries the filled ground plane, or the export step refills it; the filled B.Cu plane is what makes the five GND vias and the GND pads one net.
evidence: board_03.kicad_pcb zone block '(zone (net "GND") (layer "B.Cu") ... (fill yes (thermal_gap 0.5) ...) (polygon (pts (xy 0 0) (xy 63.5 0) (xy 63.5 45.72) (xy 0 45.72))) )' with 0 filled_polygon; kicad-cli pcb export gerbers: %TEMP%/ovl_b03/gerb_nofill/orig-B_Cu.gbl 3,795 B / 7 D01 vs gerb_check/orig-B_Cu.gbl 78,830 B / 3,032 D01; artifacts/board_03/drc.json 5x via_dangling + 4 GND unconnected_items; a scratch copy run with --refill-zones --save-board leaves only the DHT22_DATA unconnected item (10 violations, 1 unconnected).

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The request asks the board to light an LED on the same board. The design has eight components - U1 ATMEGA328P-PU, U2 DHT22, K1 SRD-05VDC-SL-C, Q1 2N2222A, D1 1N4007, R1 10k, R2 1k, C1 100nF - and NO LED, no LED net and no LED current-limiting resistor. Nothing in the artifacts says the LED was dropped; the board was emitted as if the request had been met.
expected: Either an LED and its series resistor on the board, or an explicit refusal naming that the LED could not be provided.
evidence: board_ir.json components (8 refs; attrs.package: DIP-28, DHT22, RELAY-SRD, TO-92, DO-41, AXIAL x2, RADIAL-2) and its nets (VCC_5V, GND, DHT22_DATA, TRANSISTOR_BASE, RELAY_CTRL, RELAY_COIL_NEG) - no LED net; board_03.kicad_pcb contains 8 footprints, none an LED.

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: K1's three contact pads - 3 (44.29, 19.01), 4 (44.29, 14.01), 5 (44.29, 9.01) - carry no net, and the board has no connector or terminal of any kind, so the relay's switched contacts go nowhere; only the coil (pins 1 and 2) is wired. The board cannot switch a load as delivered.
expected: The relay's COM / NO / NC contacts are brought out to a connector or terminal block, or the design states explicitly that the contacts are intentionally left open.
evidence: board_03.kicad_pcb K1: (pad "3" thru_hole ... no net), (pad "4" ... no net), (pad "5" ... no net), while (pad "1") = VCC_5V and (pad "2") = RELAY_COIL_NEG; board_ir.json K1 pads 3/4/5 net = ''.

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: VCC_5V and GND exist only on component pads. There is no connector, header or test pad anywhere on the board, so the 5 V supply has to be soldered onto a component lead (U1 pad 7 or 20) - the board has no way to be powered as delivered.
expected: A power input (connector or header) on the board edge, or a defined interface (e.g. Uno shield headers) that supplies 5 V and ground.
evidence: board_ir.json components list - the 8 parts are the only items on the board; VCC_5V's pads are U1.7, U1.20, U2.1, K1.1, D1.1, R1.1, C1.1 and GND's are U1.8, U1.22, U2.4, Q1.1, C1.2 - all component pads; no connector-type footprint exists among the 8 footprints in board_03.kicad_pcb.

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: U1's RESET (pad 1), PD0/RXD (pad 2) and PD1/TXD (pad 3) are all unconnected and there is no ICSP header on the board, so the ATmega328P cannot be programmed after assembly - no ISP and no bootloader path.
expected: Programming access: an ICSP header, or RESET + PD0 + PD1 brought out for a bootloader, with the reset pull-up/cap the datasheet's reset circuit assumes.
evidence: board_03.kicad_pcb U1 pads 1, 2 and 3 carry no (net ...); board_ir.json U1 pads 1/2/3 net = ''; no 6-pin or 2x3 header footprint among the 8 footprints.

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: U1's XTAL1 (pad 9) and XTAL2 (pad 10) are unconnected and there is no crystal or resonator on the board, so the ATmega328P has no 16 MHz timebase: with the default CKDIV8 fuse it runs the internal 8 MHz RC divided to 1 MHz, which is not the Arduino Uno the request named, and with no ISP header there is no way to set CKDIV16.
expected: A 16 MHz crystal with the two 18-22 pF load capacitors as on the Uno, or an explicit statement of the intended clock source and fuse setting.
evidence: board_03.kicad_pcb U1 pads 9 and 10 carry no (net ...); board_ir.json U1 pads 9/10 net = ''; Microchip ATmega328P default fuse CKDIV8 = programmed (1 MHz from the internal RC).

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The board carries NO silkscreen: the only graphics in the file are eight F.CrtYd courtyards, every Reference/Value property sits on F.Fab, and the exported F.Silkscreen and B.Silkscreen Gerbers contain zero draw operations (465 bytes each, 0 x D01/D02). Nothing marks which end of U1 is pin 1, which way round Q1 goes, or which end of D1 is the banded cathode. For Q1 this is not cosmetic: the 2N2222A in TO-92 is E-B-C (pin 1 = emitter, pin 2 = base, pin 3 = collector), so a part fitted back-to-front puts the emitter on RELAY_COIL_NEG and the collector on GND and the relay drive does not work.
expected: Silkscreen with component outlines, reference designators and orientation marks: a pin-1 chamfer or notch marker on U1 and Q1, a cathode band on D1, a pin-1 mark on the relay.
evidence: kicad-cli pcb export gerbers: orig-F_Silkscreen.gto and orig-B_Silkscreen.gbo 465 B, 0 draw operations; board_03.kicad_pcb contains 8 x (fp_poly ... (layer "F.CrtYd")) and no fp_text/fp_line/fp_circle on any silkscreen layer; onsemi PN2222A TO-92 pin assignment 1=Emitter 2=Base 3=Collector; KiCad Device:D convention pin 1 = cathode (banded end).

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: C1 (100 nF) is the only decoupling capacitor on the board. Its nearest pad sits 12.10 mm from U1's VCC pin 7 and 14.53 mm from U1's GND pin 8 (14.54 mm from C1 pad 1 to U1 pin 7). There is no capacitor on AVCC and none at the DHT22: C1 is 6.84 mm from U2's VCC pad and 14.20 mm from its GND pad.
expected: A 100 nF within a few millimetres of the ATmega's VCC/GND pins, a second 100 nF on AVCC, and a local 100 nF at the DHT22's supply pins.

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The request is a DHT22 on a 2 metre cable. The board offers a bare 4-pad solder footprint for the sensor (U2: 1=VCC_5V, 2=DHT22_DATA, 3=NC, 4=GND) with no connector, and the only pull-up on the data line, R1 = 10 kohm, sits on the controller board 28.40 mm from the sensor's data pad and 21.55 mm from the MCU pin. A 2 m run with the pull-up at the controller end makes the sensor's 26 us / 70 us pulse discrimination depend on the cable's capacitance; the pull-up belongs at the sensor end. The 10 kohm value itself is inside the datasheet's 5.1 kohm-for-under-30 m guidance, so the defect is where it sits, not what it is.
expected: The pull-up is fitted at the sensor end of the 2 m run (on the remote sensor board or in the cable), or the design states the decision to keep it at the controller end together with the resulting edge time.
evidence: board_03.kicad_pcb R1 (CFR-25JB-52-10K) pads (27.9, 31.79) VCC_5V and (38.06, 31.79) DHT22_DATA; U2 pad 2 at (10.12, 26.71), distance R1.2 -> U2.2 = 28.40 mm; Aosong AM2302/DHT22 datasheet: '5.1k pull-up when the connection wire is shorter than 30m, lower the resistance for longer', one-wire section ~4.7k, application figure 1k.

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The product's own drc_summary.json reports available=true, violations=15, unconnected_items=5, severity_error_violations=0, and carries no pass/fail verdict anywhere. In drc.json every one of the 5 unconnected items and both dangling DHT22_DATA tracks is filed as severity 'warning', so a reader who checks only severity_error_violations sees 0 and can read the board as clean, while the same file's unconnected_items count says five nets are open. The board was emitted anyway.
expected: The summary carries a verdict (fail when unconnected_items > 0) rather than leaving the reader to assemble one from counts, and an open circuit is not filed as a warning.
evidence: artifacts/board_03/drc_summary.json (violations 15, unconnected_items 5, severity_error_violations 0) and artifacts/board_03/drc.json (5 unconnected_items, 2 track_dangling, all severity warning) - identical to my independent kicad-cli pcb drc run at .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/board_03_drc.json (my kicad-cli run).
